text:
Sara Nguyen: Hey @People Ops — I'm planning to change my home base from the UK to Berlin on Jun 14. Quick checklist request: payroll switch, WFH stipend proration, and any tax nexus / registration risk for Redwood?
People Ops: Congrats on the move! :tada: Short answer: we'll handle payroll transfer + stipend proration, and check nexus risk. Long answer / steps below.
People Ops: 1) Please fill the 'Change of Homebase' form: https://redwoodinternal/forms/homebase-change (do this ASAP).
People Ops: 2) Submit German tax ID (Steuer-ID), local bank details, and Anmeldung once you have it. Payroll-EU-Bot has cutoffs.
Payroll-EU-Bot: Automated message — Payroll vendor: GlobalPay EU. Cutoff for June payroll: May 25 UTC. Required docs for country switch by May 20 to guarantee June pay:
```
- Passport copy (photo page)
- German tax ID (Steuer-ID) OR proof of tax registration appointment
- Local bank details (IBAN + BIC)
- Anmeldung (address registration) when available
```
People Ops: WFH stipend: prorated by days in month (we use 30-day divisor). If you move mid-month on Jun 14 we'll prorate June. Note: for payroll-country switch we sometimes need to issue a final UK payroll run and start German payroll the following month — that can affect net timing.
Thomas K.: Slightly related — when payroll switches countries, do benefits (pension contributions, employer taxes) change immediately or after a month?
People Ops: Employer contributions align to local law. In Germany, social contributions start once you are on German payroll. There can be a transitional month (final UK payslip + first German pay). We'll confirm exact dates after you submit the form.
Elaine R.: For health insurance: you usually need Anmeldung to enroll in statutory health. We partner with a local broker who helps enroll once Anmeldung + Steuer-ID are provided. If you need private coverage short-term we can help with bridging insurance.
Sara Nguyen: If Redwood does need to register a German entity for tax/workplace reasons, who flags that? I don't want my move to create extra work for the company. :thinking_face:
Legal-Team: We'll triage. Single headcount in a country generally doesn't force a company registration, but it depends on activities (sales, hiring others, permanent establishment rules). We'll do a nexus assessment if payroll headcount in DE > 1 or if you're doing sales/contracting locally. For now, proceed with homebase change; we'll monitor.
People Ops: Action items for Sara: 1) Fill the form, 2) DM payroll docs to People Ops (or upload to GlobalPay secure portal), 3) cc manager on the ticket. We'll open a p-ops ticket and loop in Legal & Payroll.
People Ops: If you want relocation assistance (moving allowance or temp housing), please email relocation@redwood.com — policy differs for EU moves vs internal transfers.
Sara Nguyen: Thanks — filing form now. One more: WFH stipend rate — does that change to EUR automatically or is it paid in GBP until payroll swap?
Payroll-EU-Bot: Currency note: payroll currency follows payroll country. Stipend paid as part of payroll will be in GBP while on UK payroll and in EUR once on German payroll. If you need a one-off currency preference, request it in the ticket.
Thomas K.: Noted, helpful.
People Ops: We'll post links in the ticket: homebase form, benefits enrollment checklist, and a short FAQ for EU moves.
Sara Nguyen: Awesome, thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
People Ops: Ping us in thread if anything blocks — we'll follow up with a ticket number within 24 hours.
